jobs.title: Director, GTM Planning & Compensation
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions to be in office minimum twice per week. (Find your Hub)
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $207,400 to $311,000 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

jobs.title: Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
jobs.description:
At Varicent, We’re Not Just Transforming The Sales Performance Management (SPM) Market—we’re Redefining How Organizations Achieve Revenue Success. Our Cutting-edge SaaS Solutions Empower Revenue Leaders Globally To Design Smarter Go-to-market Strategies, Maximize Seller Performance, And Unlock Untapped Potential. Varicent Stands At The Forefront Of Innovation, Celebrated As a Market Leader In The 2025 Forrester Wave Report For SPM, 2023 Ventana Research Revenue Performance Management (RPM) Value Index, Gartner Peer Insights, 2024 Gartner SPM Market Guide, And G2. Our Solutions Are Trusted By a Diverse Range Of Global Industry Leaders Like T-Mobile, ServiceNow, Wawanesa Bank, Shaw Industries, Moody's, Stryker And Hundreds More. Here’s Why You’ll Thrive At Varicent

Innovate with Purpose: Build impactful solutions for customers worldwide.
Join Excellence: Work in a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team.
Shape the Future: Lead in redefining revenue optimization.
Grow Together: Unlock your potential in a supportive environment.

Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Director, Digital Marketing & Web Experience
to lead how Varicent attracts, engages, and converts buyers across our digital ecosystem.

This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who loves connecting strategy with execution. You’ll own our digital growth strategy across paid media, web experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and performance measurement
, with a clear focus on generating pipeline and supporting revenue growth.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape the function — leading a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer
, partnering with specialized agencies, and working closely with senior leaders across Marketing, Sales, Revenue Operations, Product Marketing, Content, Creative, and Finance.

We’re looking for someone who is comfortable setting the vision while staying close enough to the work to know what’s performing, what isn’t, and where we should move next.

What You’ll Do

Own Our Digital Growth Strategy

Set the strategy and roadmap across paid media, website experience, SEO/AEO/GEO, conversion optimization, and digital acquisition.
Connect digital investments directly to business goals, including pipeline, revenue, customer acquisition, and brand growth.
Identify new opportunities across buyer behavior, emerging channels, AI-powered search, personalization, and digital experiences.
Bring together teams, agencies, technology, and data around clear priorities and measurable outcomes.

Turn Our Website Into a Growth Engine

Own the strategy for Varicent.com as a key demand generation, storytelling, and conversion platform.
Partner closely with our Senior Web Developer to evolve the website experience, UX, navigation, performance, accessibility, and conversion paths.
Use analytics, behavioral insights, A/B testing, and experimentation to continuously improve the buyer journey.
Lead major web initiatives such as redesigns, personalization, CMS improvements, and other digital experience programs.

Drive Digital Acquisition & Discoverability

Lead our paid media strategy across search, social, retargeting, ABM, programmatic, and other digital channels.
Own channel mix, budget allocation, forecasting, and optimization based on performance.
Shape Varicent’s approach to SEO, AEO, and GEO, helping buyers discover us across both traditional and AI-powered search experiences.
Partner with Demand Generation, Product Marketing, and Content to translate campaigns into effective digital experiences.

Make Data Actionable

Define how we measure digital performance across traffic, engagement, conversion, opportunities, pipeline, and ROI.
Partner with Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations to strengthen tracking, attribution, lead flow, and reporting.
Turn performance data into clear recommendations on where to optimize, experiment, and invest.
Build a culture of testing and continuous improvement across channels, audiences, creative, and web experiences.

Lead & Build

Lead and develop a Senior Manager of Digital Marketing and Senior Web Developer, alongside our paid media and SEO/AEO/GEO agency partners.
Create clear priorities and operating rhythms that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing quality.
Own digital marketing and web budgets, agency relationships, tools, and investments.
Serve as a trusted digital strategy partner to the SVP of Marketing and broader Marketing leadership team.
Help shape how the digital and web function evolves as Varicent grows.

What You’ll Bring

We’re looking for a digital leader who has operated in a B2B SaaS, technology, enterprise software, or similarly complex sales environment
and understands how digital experiences translate into business growth.

You’ll Likely Bring

12+ years of experience across digital marketing, growth, demand generation, performance marketing, or web strategy.
7+ years of people leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams or managers.
Experience owning digital strategy with measurable responsibility for pipeline, revenue, conversion, and customer acquisition.
Deep knowledge of paid media, SEO/SEM, digital acquisition, web strategy, CRO, analytics, and experimentation.
Experience owning or significantly influencing a B2B website and understanding how UX, content, technology, and conversion work together.
Experience managing meaningful digital budgets and making investment decisions based on performance.
Strong analytical instincts and the ability to turn complex data into clear recommendations.
Experience leading agencies and external partners while maintaining strong internal ownership.
The ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and connect digital strategy to broader company goals.
Comfort working in a growth-oriented environment where priorities evolve and leaders are expected to both set direction and help move the work forward.
Familiarity with tools such as HubSpot, Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, Salesforce, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, ABM platforms, experimentation tools, and modern analytics platforms.
An understanding of how AI is changing digital marketing, content discovery, personalization, and the buyer journey.

Nice to Have

Experience with HubSpot CMS, ABM and intent platforms, multi-touch attribution, website personalization, CRO platforms, behavioral analytics, major website redesigns or migrations, and global digital programs
is a plus.

Working knowledge of HTML/CSS and familiarity with accessibility, privacy, Core Web Vitals, and web governance will also help you partner effectively with our web team.

What Success Looks Like

In your first few months, you’ll get to know our digital ecosystem, team, agencies, performance, and buyers; identify where we can improve quickly; and establish clear priorities for digital growth.

From there, you’ll build a multi-quarter roadmap, strengthen how we measure digital contribution to pipeline and revenue, establish a structured experimentation approach, and evolve Varicent’s website into an even stronger growth and conversion engine.

Over time, success will mean better digital experiences, stronger organic visibility, smarter media investment, higher conversion, clearer performance insights, and measurable growth in digital-sourced pipeline
— supported by a team and operating model that can scale with Varicent.

Additional Information

For this role, the estimated annual base salary range is between $138,200.00 - $181,400.00 CAD
. In addition to base salary, our compensation package may include bonuses, commissions for eligible sales roles, and a comprehensive benefits package. The actual base salary will vary based on factors including individual qualifications and market data, as objectively assessed during the interview process.

This posting is for a new vacancy
.

This hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement — not replace — human decision-making.

Overview Of Benefits

Health & Wellness — Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage tailored to your local needs
Time Off — PTO and public holidays to rest, recharge, and do what matters most
Volunteer Days — Dedicated time to give back and support the communities that matter to you
Ignite Days — Dedicated learning days to support continuous growth, skill development, and professional learning
Financial — Compensation that reflects your market and your value
Retirement — Retirement plans designed to help you build long-term financial security
Tuition Assistance — Invest in your growth with support for continuing education and professional development
Flexibility — Work where you thrive, with remote and hybrid options available across most regions

Varicent is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. If you require accommodation at any time during the recruitment process please email accomodations@varicent.com

Varicent is also committed to compliance with all fair employment practices regarding citizenship and immigration status. jobs.description:

Toronto, Canada

up to $250,000, dependent on experience
Employment:
Permanent | Full-time
Industry:
Legal & Professional Services

Ingenio is supporting a leading international law firm with the appointment of a Global Head of Digital Strategy & Transformation
.

This is a senior leadership position reporting directly to the Global Chief Operating Officer, with significant exposure to the Board and wider executive leadership team. The successful candidate will lead the firm's digital transformation strategy, bringing together business applications, data, AI, automation and digital client services to deliver measurable business improvements.

This is not a traditional IT infrastructure or operational technology role. An established CTO is responsible for those areas. The focus of this appointment is on strategy, development, transformation and execution
.

The Opportunity
You will take responsibility for developing and delivering a global digital transformation strategy across legal, corporate and trust services. Working with senior business stakeholders, you will turn commercial and operational challenges into practical technology solutions that improve efficiency, client experience and service delivery.

You'll inherit an established application development team and will be responsible for developing its capabilities as the transformation programme progresses.

Significant projects are already underway, including a major entity-management platform initiative, a broader data management and analytics programme, and opportunities to extend the use of AI and automation across the business.

Key Responsibilities
Develop and deliver a global digital strategy and transformation roadmap aligned with business priorities.
Lead and develop the existing Business Technology and Application Development team.
Own the business applications roadmap, including entity management and client-facing technology solutions.
Oversee the design, development and delivery of new systems, whether built internally, purchased or delivered through external partners.
Drive the data strategy, analytics, reporting and business intelligence agenda.
Identify and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across legal and professional services.

What We're Looking For
We are particularly interested in senior digital transformation and business technology leaders from professional services, legal, fiduciary/corporate services, financial services or similarly complex, regulated environments
.

You will bring:
Significant experience leading digital strategy, business technology or enterprise transformation.
A proven track record of delivering complex technology programmes with measurable business outcomes.
Strong experience across business applications, software development and technology-enabled process improvement.
A solid understanding of data strategy, analytics, business intelligence, AI and automation.
Experience leading multidisciplinary development teams and managing external delivery partners.
The ability to influence Board-level stakeholders while remaining technically credible and close to delivery.

Location & Package
Toronto is the mandatory location, with this being an in-office role.

Interested?
This is an opportunity to shape the digital direction of an established international professional services organisation, with direct access to senior leadership, an existing development capability and significant transformation programmes already underway.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Michelle Queally at Ingenio
, or apply directly.

jobs.title: Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap
jobs.description:
Job Description

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

Your responsibilities will include:

Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale
Stakeholder intake: Capturing, assessing, and prioritizing feature requests from business lines, users, and leadership against a consistent value bar
User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.
Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions
Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome
Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates
Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms
Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.
Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration
Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes
Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry
Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code
Have agile delivery expertise: backlog grooming and acceptance-criteria definition
Have financial services awareness, or the ability to develop it quickly - understanding banking end-users (advisors, analysts, operations staff) and their workflow needs

Nice to have:

Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, HCI, or a related discipline
Product management certification (AIPM, Pragmatic Institute, CSPO, or SAFe)
Experience building developer platforms, APIs, or self-service builder tools
Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OSFI E-23, or equivalent)
Experience with prompt engineering, model evaluation, or fine-tuning in production
Background at a fintech, regtech, or major bank digital team

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment:

RBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors. Disability-related accommodations during the application process are available upon request.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions to be in office minimum twice per week. (Find your Hub)
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $207,400 to $311,000 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Compensation: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Operations Finance
jobs.description:
Job Summary

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Vice President, Operations Finance, the Senior Director, Operations Finance owns operational accounting for Live Nation Canada. This is the senior operating leader of a function that accounts for every show, venue and festival we run in this country; tens of thousands of transactions a year, settled under contract in a fast-paced environment where the work is visible and the stakes are real.

The Senior Director’s mission will be to elevate the function by building a high-performing team and setting standards nationally for how shows and venues are accounted for. They will be responsible to evolve current processes toward greater automation, control and scale. Success in the first 12 months will be clear and measurable: a functioning management layer that consistently delivers on deadlines; a faster, cleaner close with a defensible timetable and fewer post-close adjustments; one written national process standard in use across all markets; an automated end-to-end workflow that is live, adopted and measurably reducing manual effort or error; and a strong control environment where audit findings are closed promptly and none repeat. Working in close partnership with the Vice President, the Senior Director will help shape the direction and priorities of the function. They will be the trusted go-to partner for the business on all matters of operational accounting.

This is a great opportunity to own a national function, build a team around it, and elevate how Live Nation Canada does its accounting.

What This Role Will Do

Leadership

Own the structure, capability and performance of a ~12-person operational accounting team spanning show settlement, venue accounting and financial close
Lead through managers: develop the management layer, set clear ownership accountabilities, establish performance standards and hold managers accountable for their teams' deadlines and quality
Own talent strategy for the function: hiring standards, onboarding, development plans, succession depth, and a coverage model that holds through peak season, festival periods and major tours

Event Reporting and Operational Accounting

Accountable for the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of all events, venues and festivals accounting nationally (including the integrity of reported contribution margin by show, venue and market)
Own the close calendar end to end and commit to the timetable; ensure corporate reporting deadlines are consistently met
Own the accounting treatment of show settlement: from artist final settlements against contract, withholding tax, charity and merchandise/bundle recognition, co-promoted events, joint venture splits, venue expense settlement and shared ancillary revenue
Own accounting for owned and operated venues, including inventory, labour costs and cash handling
Own balance sheet integrity for the function: reconciliation quality, accrual adequacy, deferred revenue, AR aging and collections performance for event-related balances
Develop and recommend accounting positions on complex deal structures such as co-promoted events, joint ventures, festival vehicles, rental versus promoted, international artist withholding, multi-year ancillary agreements
Partner with regional controllers to ensure consistent application of policy across markets, and resolve differences rather than reporting them
Partner with VP, Operational Accounting and Corporate for all technical accounting approval
Accountable for the day-to-day operation of internal controls over settlement, cash floats, AP approval and wire release, including SOX-relevant controls in scope
Play a critical role in internal and external audits; owning remediation of findings to closure while ensuring every settlement is audit-ready with proper documentation backup
Proactively identify control gaps as volume, venues and deal structures change, and implement corrective action

National Responsibilities

Develop, implement and sustain a national operational accounting playbook: settlement process, documentation standards, close process and checklist, reconciliation methodology, escalation path.
Identify and improve workstreams end to end; from business case through delivery to adoption and measured benefit
Define and report the function's operating metrics: days to close, settlement cycle time, restatement and error rates, aged AR, control exception volume. Use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement
Own the data standards that allow event economics to be reported consistently

Partner with the business

Provide the actuals, trend data and event-level insight that Strategic Finance and FP&A build the budget and forecast on; accountable for the reliability of what they plan from
Support due diligence, integration planning and post-close financial integration
Deputize for the VP, Operational Accounting on function matters with senior leadership to set priorities for the function, and act as their delegate with senior leadership when needed

What This Person Will Bring

CPA designation required; Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field
10–12 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including experience leading managers and building a management layer, not only managing individual contributors
Demonstrated ownership of a close and control environment across multiple sites, markets or entities within a larger corporate finance organization
A track record of leading a process or systems improvement end to end, from business case through delivery and adoption to measured result
Live entertainment, hospitality, venue, sports or comparable high-volume, deal-driven, contract-settled environment strongly preferred; comfort with a pace where revenue is earned in a single night and settled quickly
Strong Oracle and/or Salesforce capability; advanced Excel; practical use of Claude, AI platforms, BI and automation tooling to reduce manual work
Ability to hold an accounting position under commercial pressure while keeping the relationship intact
Credibility and presence with senior commercial leadership; able to explain complex financial outcomes clearly to non-financial stakeholders and earn their trust
Resourceful and hands-on when it matters; this is a senior role embedded in an operating business
Availability for travel and on-site support for major shows and festival properties, including evenings and weekends during peak season

Benefits & Perks

Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits:

HEALTH: Medical, Dental and Vision benefits for you and your family, along with Employee Assistance Programs through Modern Health and ComPsych
YOURSELF: Generous paid time off policy including holiday closures, and sick time for you and dependents, along with free concert tickets
WEALTH: RRSP program with company match, Stock Program Reimbursement
FAMILY: New parent programs & support including caregiver leave and baby bonus, and infertility support
CAREER: Tuition reimbursement, student loan repayment, and internal growth and development programs and training
OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding network, gender reassignment support

We thank all candidates for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

--

The expected compensation for this position in Ontario is: $156,000-195,000

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

Sits for extended periods of time at a computer station or work desk; stands and walks throughout the day; occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.; uses hands and fingers to operate computers and office equipment for up to 8 hours each day; lifts up to 10 pounds regularly; exposed to typical office environment conditions and noise levels.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We are passionate and committed to our people and go beyond the rhetoric of diversity and inclusion. You will be working in an inclusive environment and be encouraged to bring your whole self to work. We will do all that we can to help you successfully balance your work and homelife. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with. It’s talent that matters to us and we encourage applications from people irrespective of their gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability status or caring responsibilities.

Live Nation strongly supports equal employment opportunity for all applicants regardless of age (40 and over), ancestry, color, religious creed (including religious dress and grooming practices), family and medical care leave or the denial of family and medical care leave, mental or physical disability (including HIV and AIDS), marital status, domestic partner status, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), genetic information, military and veteran status, political affiliation, national origin (including language use restrictions), citizenship, race, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding), gender, gender identity, and gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law, rule, ordinance or regulation.

We also afford equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with a disability. For this reason, Live Nation will make reasonable accommodations for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability who is an applicant consistent with its legal obligations to do so, including reasonable accommodations related to pregnancy in accordance with applicable local, provincial and / or federal law. As part of its commitment to make reasonable accommodations, Live Nation also wishes to participate in a timely, good faith, interactive process with a disabled applicant to determine effective reasonable accommodations, if any, which can be made in response to a request for accommodations. Applicants are invited to identify reasonable accommodations that can be made to assist them to perform the essential functions of the position they seek. Any applicant who requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of the job should contact a Human Resources Representative to request the opportunity to participate in a timely interactive process. Live Nation will also provide reasonable religious accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

HIRING PRACTICES

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Operations Finance
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Vice President, Operations Finance, the Senior Director, Operations Finance owns operational accounting for Live Nation Canada. This is the senior operating leader of a function that accounts for every show, venue and festival we run in this country; tens of thousands of transactions a year, settled under contract in a fast-paced environment where the work is visible and the stakes are real.

The Senior Director’s mission will be to elevate the function by building a high-performing team and setting standards nationally for how shows and venues are accounted for. They will be responsible to evolve current processes toward greater automation, control and scale. Success in the first 12 months will be clear and measurable: a functioning management layer that consistently delivers on deadlines; a faster, cleaner close with a defensible timetable and fewer post-close adjustments; one written national process standard in use across all markets; an automated end-to-end workflow that is live, adopted and measurably reducing manual effort or error; and a strong control environment where audit findings are closed promptly and none repeat. Working in close partnership with the Vice President, the Senior Director will help shape the direction and priorities of the function. They will be the trusted go-to partner for the business on all matters of operational accounting.

This is a great opportunity to own a national function, build a team around it, and elevate how Live Nation Canada does its accounting.

What This Role Will Do

Leadership

Own the structure, capability and performance of a ~12-person operational accounting team spanning show settlement, venue accounting and financial close
Lead through managers: develop the management layer, set clear ownership accountabilities, establish performance standards and hold managers accountable for their teams' deadlines and quality
Own talent strategy for the function: hiring standards, onboarding, development plans, succession depth, and a coverage model that holds through peak season, festival periods and major tours

Event Reporting and Operational Accounting

Accountable for the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of all events, venues and festivals accounting nationally (including the integrity of reported contribution margin by show, venue and market)
Own the close calendar end to end and commit to the timetable; ensure corporate reporting deadlines are consistently met
Own the accounting treatment of show settlement: from artist final settlements against contract, withholding tax, charity and merchandise/bundle recognition, co-promoted events, joint venture splits, venue expense settlement and shared ancillary revenue
Own accounting for owned and operated venues, including inventory, labour costs and cash handling
Own balance sheet integrity for the function: reconciliation quality, accrual adequacy, deferred revenue, AR aging and collections performance for event-related balances
Develop and recommend accounting positions on complex deal structures such as co-promoted events, joint ventures, festival vehicles, rental versus promoted, international artist withholding, multi-year ancillary agreements
Partner with regional controllers to ensure consistent application of policy across markets, and resolve differences rather than reporting them
Partner with VP, Operational Accounting and Corporate for all technical accounting approval
Accountable for the day-to-day operation of internal controls over settlement, cash floats, AP approval and wire release, including SOX-relevant controls in scope
Play a critical role in internal and external audits; owning remediation of findings to closure while ensuring every settlement is audit-ready with proper documentation backup
Proactively identify control gaps as volume, venues and deal structures change, and implement corrective action

National Responsibilities

Develop, implement and sustain a national operational accounting playbook: settlement process, documentation standards, close process and checklist, reconciliation methodology, escalation path.
Identify and improve workstreams end to end; from business case through delivery to adoption and measured benefit
Define and report the function's operating metrics: days to close, settlement cycle time, restatement and error rates, aged AR, control exception volume. Use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement
Own the data standards that allow event economics to be reported consistently

Partner with the business

Provide the actuals, trend data and event-level insight that Strategic Finance and FP&A build the budget and forecast on; accountable for the reliability of what they plan from
Support due diligence, integration planning and post-close financial integration
Deputize for the VP, Operational Accounting on function matters with senior leadership to set priorities for the function, and act as their delegate with senior leadership when needed

What This Person Will Bring

CPA designation required; Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field
10–12 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including experience leading managers and building a management layer, not only managing individual contributors
Demonstrated ownership of a close and control environment across multiple sites, markets or entities within a larger corporate finance organization
A track record of leading a process or systems improvement end to end, from business case through delivery and adoption to measured result
Live entertainment, hospitality, venue, sports or comparable high-volume, deal-driven, contract-settled environment strongly preferred; comfort with a pace where revenue is earned in a single night and settled quickly
Strong Oracle and/or Salesforce capability; advanced Excel; practical use of Claude, AI platforms, BI and automation tooling to reduce manual work
Ability to hold an accounting position under commercial pressure while keeping the relationship intact
Credibility and presence with senior commercial leadership; able to explain complex financial outcomes clearly to non-financial stakeholders and earn their trust
Resourceful and hands-on when it matters; this is a senior role embedded in an operating business
Availability for travel and on-site support for major shows and festival properties, including evenings and weekends during peak season

Benefits & Perks

Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits:

HEALTH: Medical, Dental and Vision benefits for you and your family, along with Employee Assistance Programs through Modern Health and ComPsych
YOURSELF: Generous paid time off policy including holiday closures, and sick time for you and dependents, along with free concert tickets
WEALTH: RRSP program with company match, Stock Program Reimbursement
FAMILY: New parent programs & support including caregiver leave and baby bonus, and infertility support
CAREER: Tuition reimbursement, student loan repayment, and internal growth and development programs and training
OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding network, gender reassignment support

We thank all candidates for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

--

The expected compensation for this position in Ontario is: $156,000-195,000

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

Sits for extended periods of time at a computer station or work desk; stands and walks throughout the day; occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.; uses hands and fingers to operate computers and office equipment for up to 8 hours each day; lifts up to 10 pounds regularly; exposed to typical office environment conditions and noise levels.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We are passionate and committed to our people and go beyond the rhetoric of diversity and inclusion. You will be working in an inclusive environment and be encouraged to bring your whole self to work. We will do all that we can to help you successfully balance your work and homelife. As a growing business we will encourage you to develop your professional and personal aspirations, enjoy new experiences, and learn from the talented people you will be working with. It’s talent that matters to us and we encourage applications from people irrespective of their gender, race, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability status or caring responsibilities.

Live Nation strongly supports equal employment opportunity for all applicants regardless of age (40 and over), ancestry, color, religious creed (including religious dress and grooming practices), family and medical care leave or the denial of family and medical care leave, mental or physical disability (including HIV and AIDS), marital status, domestic partner status, medical condition (including cancer and genetic characteristics), genetic information, military and veteran status, political affiliation, national origin (including language use restrictions), citizenship, race, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding), gender, gender identity, and gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law, rule, ordinance or regulation.

We also afford equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with a disability. For this reason, Live Nation will make reasonable accommodations for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability who is an applicant consistent with its legal obligations to do so, including reasonable accommodations related to pregnancy in accordance with applicable local, provincial and / or federal law. As part of its commitment to make reasonable accommodations, Live Nation also wishes to participate in a timely, good faith, interactive process with a disabled applicant to determine effective reasonable accommodations, if any, which can be made in response to a request for accommodations. Applicants are invited to identify reasonable accommodations that can be made to assist them to perform the essential functions of the position they seek. Any applicant who requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential functions of the job should contact a Human Resources Representative to request the opportunity to participate in a timely interactive process. Live Nation will also provide reasonable religious accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

HIRING PRACTICES

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job
